To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
- The susceptibility to SCC is strongly influenced by the loading history and the pre-strain level.

the effect of the pre-strain level is significant on the SCC crack initiation susceptibility of austenitic stainless steels, that the effect of pre-deformation mode is also significant, and that the SCC crack initiation behavior is mainly governed by the deformation mode.
- The susceptibility of austenitic stainless steels to IGSCC is strongly influenced by the deformation mode and the deformation history of the material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of prior deformation on the initiation and growth of stress corrosion cracks in austenitic stainless steels.
the influence of cold working on the SCC initiation of austenitic stainless steel welds in simulated primary PWR water.
the influence of the deformation mode on the SCC susceptibility of AISI 304L and 316L stainless steel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pre-straining of austenitic stainless steels by cold rolling and cold drawing increases the susceptibility of these materials to SCC in simulated PWR primary water.
the effect of cold working on the initiation of IGSCC of 316L austenitic stainless steels is a complex function of the cold working mode and the cold working intensity.
the effect of pre deformation by rolling on the susceptibility to SCC is more important than the effect of pre strain by tension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the susceptibility of the austenitic stainless steels to SCC is controlled by the strain hardening of the materials and by the stress intensity factor.
the pre-straining effect on SCC initiation is mainly due to the effect of deformation path.
the effect of the deformation path on the susceptibility to initiation of SCC for AISI 304L and 316L austenitic stainless steels is significant and cannot be neglected.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effect of pre-strain on the susceptibility to IGC is not straightforward and is strongly dependent on the pre-strain mode and the strain path, which should be taken into account in the assessment of the susceptibility to IGG in pre-strained stainless steel components.
the effect of the strain path on the initiation of SCC in austenitic stainless steels is not a function of the prestrain level.

the austenitic stainless steels are susceptible to SCC in simulated primary water at temperatures between 290degC and 360degC, and that the susceptibility to SCC is strongly influenced by the strain history of the material, regardless of whether the steel is solution annealed, prestrained or preformed.
